clue.text: Handout from salesman functions to stop people carriers beginning to depreciate

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so one piece is pushed into the middle of the vehicles

parts.note: a bus and a car are both vehicles that carry people
sines are trigonometric functions

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of depreciate is used

explanation.surface: A salesman's leaflet is about how to stop people carriers losing value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' looks like a verb for the salesman, but it means the trigonometric kind; 'to stop' plugs them into the first vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman hands out a small printed card bearing name and contact details.

clue.text: Wave Muppet Republican inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the Republican letter is placed within the Muppet's name

parts.note: Beaker is the lab assistant Muppet

explanation.surface: A Muppet character waves while a Republican sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wave crashing into foam on the shore is called this.

clue.text: Decorated column found in wasteland

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters sit concealed inside the word wasteland

explanation.surface: An ornate pillar turns up in an empty wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright stone slab or pillar carved with inscriptions or designs, as in ancient monuments.

clue.text: Trip often, scattering remaining income

indicators.note: scattering the letters of trip often throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trips frequently and drops what is left of their earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings left over after all costs and expenses are deducted from revenue.

clue.text: Temperature dropped in hot water layer

indicators.note: dropped means the temperature letter is taken away from the vapour word

parts.note: steam is hot water in vapour form

explanation.surface: A temperature fall in hot water forms a distinct layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum of coal or ore running through rock is a geological layer.

clue.text: Song is able to delight passing king

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: passing here means skipping over, so the king's letter is left out of the delight word

parts.note: to tickle is to delight or amuse
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A song can please a king who happens to be passing by.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or chant, especially one with words taken from the Bible, used in church services.

clue.text: Strange graduate's dance

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or odd
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate performs an odd dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance in quick rhythm with hip movements.

clue.text: Former doorman is overseas trader

parts.note: ex means former
a porter guards the door of a building

explanation.surface: A one-time doorman has become an international merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells goods to buyers in other countries trades abroad.

clue.text: Points repeatedly to nurse close to collapse after advanced test

indicators.note: after means the advanced letter comes first, followed by the rest
to nurse is to hold close, so the points wrap round a single letter
repeatedly means the pair of points is given twice

parts.note: S and S are two compass points, south

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of collapse

explanation.surface: After an advanced exam, someone keeps telling a nurse that a collapse is near.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or appraise something, as an examiner does with a candidate.

clue.text: European certainly next to file complaint

indicators.note: next to says the pieces are placed side by side in order

parts.note: yes, certainly, as an answer
a file of people or vehicles can be a train, a line

explanation.surface: A European is happy to file a formal complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense: tired, sore eyes from overuse.

clue.text: Old cars overturned early in the morning

indicators.note: overturned means the time phrase is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: six a.m. is early in the morning

explanation.surface: Classic cars found upside down at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Austin Maxi was a British family car of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maxi was a hatchback made by Austin; the plural names several such vintage models.

clue.text: Greetings from regulars in Ukrainian powerboat

indicators.note: regulars in tells us to take letters at a regular interval, every third one starting from the second

explanation.surface: Hellos are shouted from a Ukrainian speedboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The pick is every third letter starting with the K of Ukrainian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maori greeting used in New Zealand, wishing good health.

clue.text: Long to accept piece of advice in place of PPE?

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so the yearning word encloses other letters

parts.note: to long for is to pine

indicators.note: a piece of a word is here its first letter

parts.note: for can mean in place of, as in substituting one for another

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for advice on what to wear in place of safety gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless apron-like garment that protects clothing, a homely kind of protective equipment.

clue.text: Trump will accept no tiebreaker

indicators.note: will accept means the trumping word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: in card games, to ruff is to play a trump

explanation.surface: Donald Trump will not accept a deciding second vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding extra race or second round of voting held when the first is tied.

clue.text: Mostly employ Union to replace insurgents, initially, after an uprising in submarine

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later in the answer
in a down clue an uprising means the word is read from bottom to top
to replace means one letter is swapped in where another stood
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to utilise is to employ

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of insurgents

explanation.surface: An insurgent uprising on a submarine is put down with the help of a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims UTILISE to UTILIS, then U takes the place of its second I to give UTILUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo's underwater vessel in Jules Verne, and the first nuclear-powered sub.

clue.text: Colourful plant found in Sweden after climate changed

indicators.note: after means the Sweden letter follows the rearranged letters
changed means the letters of climate are put in a different order

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A bright flower is discovered in Sweden once the climate shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing shrub with showy flowers in purple, pink or white.

clue.text: Smoker returned an offensive letter from Athens after a short time

indicators.note: after means the short time piece comes first, with the rest following it

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

indicators.note: returned means these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a major 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A smoker sends back an offensive letter from Greece after a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's active volcano, which smokes and erupts, so cryptically a smoker.

clue.text: Person who won't worship Etruscan bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of Etruscan are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An Etruscan bust depicts a non-believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture to go with Etruscan, but signals breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, someone who refused to attend Church of England services.

clue.text: Relatively short and thick uninvited guest

definitions.meaning: more stocky and dumpy, a comparative adjective
someone occupying a building without permission

explanation.surface: A rather stocky person turns up without an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning stocky, and also someone who occupies property unlawfully.

clue.text: Mixture of wee, gas and effluent

indicators.note: a mixture of the letters means they are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Urine and gas mixed together make waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste water and excrement carried away in drains is liquid effluent.

clue.text: Mug with drink for old copper

parts.note: a mug is a kind of cup
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A mug of rum is offered to a retired policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; the Latin name gives the symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for the metal Cu, an old term once used by chemists.

clue.text: Mongoose is reportedly only pet

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: mere cat means only a pet, a mere moggy

explanation.surface: A mongoose is said to be nothing more than a household pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing African carnivore belonging to the mongoose family.

clue.text: What's the reason to push audibly in heavy snowfall?

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: why means what's the reason, and to tout is to push or promote goods

explanation.surface: Someone asks why bother pushing through a blizzard.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard so dense that the horizon and landscape vanish into white.

clue.text: Obscene magazine shows medical procedure

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display inside obscene magazine

explanation.surface: A dirty magazine depicts a hospital treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Injecting fluid into the rectum to clear the bowels.

clue.text: Model that's still law, with time running out

indicators.note: running out means the time letter leaves the law word

parts.note: a statute is a written law

explanation.surface: A model posing motionless while a law expires.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure, a likeness that never moves.

clue.text: Exchange rubbish vehicle

definitions.meaning: to barter or trade, an old sense
worthless odds and ends, a dated sense
a lorry or large goods motor

explanation.surface: Swap the bin lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: to barter goods, worthless odds and ends, and a goods lorry.

clue.text: Counterfeit bar of chocolate left out

indicators.note: out means the left letter is removed from the chocolate bar

parts.note: a Flake is a crumbly Cadbury chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Fake chocolate bars are left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Flake is a British Cadbury chocolate bar of thin crumbly folds.
explanation.definitionFit: A forged item, or as an adjective sham, not genuine.

clue.text: University dons joke before English test

indicators.note: before means the joke piece comes ahead of the English letter
dons means puts on, here read as the joke being worn around the university letter

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: University lecturers make a quip before an English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university tutors but works as an insertion verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure or estimate, as in judging the mood of a crowd.

clue.text: American football authority baffled about British making easy money

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

indicators.note: about means the baffled word goes around the British letter

parts.note: stuck means baffled, unable to proceed

explanation.surface: The US football body is puzzled by Britain making quick profits.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for money earned quickly and with little effort, often dubiously.

clue.text: Stock exchange in court over former PM accepting obsolete currency

indicators.note: in means the prime minister piece goes inside the court letters
accepting means the former leader takes the old currency inside his name

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British prime minister from 1945 to 1951
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A former prime minister in court takes old money from the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where livestock are bought and sold, punning on the financial institution.
